### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A34 was about 1 hour (median ~1.0 h, quartiles ~0.9–1.1 h); in the later window it was about 2 hours (median ~2.0 h, quartiles ~1.8–2.2 h), a mean increase of roughly 1 hour. This pair was observed in all 200 traces in both windows. [TWAIT001]
- The same doubling appears for the pairs A35→A34 (median ~0.98 h → ~2.0 h) and A37→A34 (median ~1.04 h → ~1.97 h), so all three measured intervals into A34 roughly doubled. [TWAIT002, TWAIT003]
- The spread of these elapsed times also about doubled (standard deviation from ~0.16 h to ~0.31–0.35 h), and the whole distribution shifted up — all quartiles rose by roughly 0.8–1.1 hours — rather than only the slowest cases becoming slower. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003]
- The consecutive pairs A35→A34 and A37→A34 were observed somewhat less often in the later window (about 76→66 and 82→52 out of 200 traces), but no control-flow difference passed the screening thresholds (0 items against about 0.31 expected by chance), so this may be sampling variation. [TWAIT002, TWAIT003]
- Each of the three time differences is larger than about 999.5 in 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data; the time family produced 3 qualifying items where about 0.01 would be expected if nothing had changed, while the control-flow family produced 0 against about 0.31 expected. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a timing change around activity A34: in the later window, the elapsed time from the completion of its predecessors A26, A35 and A37 to the completion of A34 is about one hour longer than before, roughly doubling from about 1 hour to about 2 hours, with the entire distribution shifted upward and variability about doubled. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003]

Supporting signs: the shift is measured directly by the timing indicator on three transitions into the same activity, all agreeing in direction and magnitude, which is consistent with a single timing change around A34 rather than unrelated fluctuations; the time family yielded 3 qualifying items against about 0.01 expected without a change, so chance is an unlikely explanation for the set; and the doubling also holds on the A26→A34 pair, observed in every trace in both windows, so it is not confined to a shrinking subset of cases. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003]

Limitations and competing explanation: T_WAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting or service time, so the extra hour may lie in the predecessors' completion timing or in work between the events rather than at A34 itself. The lower counts of consecutive A35→A34 and A37→A34 pairs could reflect changed adjacency, which would alter which events get paired; the control-flow screening found no qualifying structural difference (0 items against about 0.31 expected), but it cannot fully rule this out. [TWAIT002, TWAIT003]
